logline: The murder of an eleven-year-old boy in a small Dorset coastal town forces two detectives and an entire community to confront what they thought they knew about their neighbours - and themselves.

renewal.note: Creator Chris Chibnall confirmed the show was always conceived as a three-series trilogy and ruled out any continuation in 2019.

bollymeter.basis: 94 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 36 reviews; Metacritic 91; IMDb 8.3. Won BAFTA Best Drama 2013. Critics called it one of the finest pieces of British television of its decade.

pull_quotes.text: Well written and beautifully shot, Broadchurch is a deliberate, slowly unfolding mystery with terrific performances.

seasons.review_body: Series 1 aired on ITV in March 2013, earning 94 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 36 critics and 91 on Metacritic. It won the BAFTA for Best Drama Series and was named best TV series of 2013 by Radio Times. David Tennant as the abrasive, chronically ill DI Alec Hardy and Olivia Colman as the community-embedded DS Ellie Miller were praised as one of the great detective pairings in British television history. Chris Chibnall's writing was singled out for making the procedural investigation emotionally consequential: the who of the murder mattered less than what the investigation cost the town. The Guardian ranked it eleventh in its list of the 100 best TV shows of the 21st century. The Dorset cliff setting became as recognisable as the performances.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: The Broadchurch premiere opens on the finding of an eleven-year-old boy's body on a Dorset beach, and Chris Chibnall's script makes an immediate structural decision: the investigation is secondary to the community's grief. The procedural machinery - detective pairings, press intrusion, family liaison - is present and precisely observed, but Broadchurch's first episode establishes that what the show is actually about is what violence does to a place that thought itself safe. David Tennant as the imported DI Alec Hardy is positioned as professionally effective and personally opaque; Olivia Colman as DS Ellie Miller is positioned as locally rooted and professionally underestimated. The tension between their operating modes is the drama's engine. James Strong's direction is unhurried and visually precise about the Dorset landscape - the cliffs, the sea, the town's smallness - which will be as load-bearing as either lead performance in what follows.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The body of eleven-year-old Danny Latimer is found on the beach at Broadchurch, and the arrival of outsider DI Alec Hardy disrupts DS Ellie Miller's expected promotion while shattering the town's self-image as a safe community. The premiere is precise and unhurried, establishing grief as the season's real subject before the investigation has properly begun.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment Danny's father learns the news - a scene that set the emotional register for every episode that followed.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 8
episode_reviews.review_body: The Broadchurch Series 1 finale resolves what eight weeks of community grief had built toward, and Chibnall's choice of killer serves the show's consistent argument about hidden lives within places that believe they know everyone. The procedural revelation is almost structurally secondary to its emotional aftermath - the finale is longest and most sustained in its examination of what the answer costs the people closest to it. Olivia Colman's work in the final episode was cited by the BAFTA judges, Radio Times critics, and Guardian television critics as among the finest single-episode performances of the year. David Tennant's handling of Hardy's own disclosure - a secret held throughout the season that the finale deploys at the moment of maximum investment - arrives as a structural counterweight to the investigation's conclusion. Broadchurch's Series 1 finale was watched by 10.5 million UK viewers, ITV's highest drama audience in years, and was repeated within a week to an additional audience of 3.5 million.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale reveals Danny's killer and pays off eight weeks of accumulated community grief. Critics who had followed the series noted that Chibnall's choice of killer served the show's themes about hidden lives within closed communities. Olivia Colman's reaction to the revelation was cited as one of the most powerful single moments in the series' run.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Ellie Miller's confrontation with the truth - Olivia Colman's best work in a season full of it.

bollymeter.basis: 84 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 30 reviews; Metacritic 73. Critics praised the courtroom expansion but noted the season worked less well as standalone mystery, relying heavily on Series 1 investment.

seasons.review_body: Series 2 aired in January 2015. The season opened the Danny Latimer case to a criminal trial while simultaneously excavating a past case of Hardy's involving allegations of rape. The courtroom expansion brings a richer scope, and new cast members join the story smoothly. The season structure leans on groundwork laid in Series 1, with the central relationship between Hardy and Miller continuing to drive the show forward. Both Tennant and Colman deliver standout work again. The season lands as a strong continuation, though it does not consistently match Series 1's peak critical impact, a typical challenge for follow ups to landmark mystery procedurals.
seasons.season_over_season: The courtroom setting gave the story a new procedural grammar, but the season operated as aftermath rather than standalone mystery, limiting its critical ceiling compared to Series 1.

bollymeter.basis: 98 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 43 reviews; Metacritic 85. Critics called it a return to form that matched and some said exceeded Series 1, with its handling of a sexual assault investigation receiving particular praise.

pull_quotes.text: Combines socially conscious themes with suspenseful mystery and a pair of compelling leads.

seasons.review_body: The final series aired in February 2017, reaching 98 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 43 reviews and 85 on Metacritic, the highest Metacritic score in the trilogy. The season centers on a sexual assault rather than a murder, and Chibnall’s writing approaches the survivor experience with a serious, non-exploitative tone. Hardy and Miller return as the leads, while the Rotten Tomatoes consensus frames the show as a high standard for police procedurals that blends social consciousness with suspenseful mystery. The social-issues framing can feel slightly didactic, yet Series 3 plays as a genuine creative recovery and a worthy conclusion to the trilogy. The IMDb audience score sits slightly lower than Series 1 and 2, reflecting some ambivalence about the tonal shift.
seasons.season_over_season: A complete subject change - from murder to sexual assault investigation - gave the series fresh purpose and earned its best Metacritic score, recovering fully from the critical dip of Series 2.
